claims.text: The target material is a multi-principal refractory alloy based on elements such as Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, and W with a primary BCC solid-solution phase.
High-throughput computational screening can efficiently narrow the large composition space for strong, ductile, lightweight RHEAs.
The proposed screening workflow integrates CALPHAD-based thermodynamic assessments.
The proposed screening workflow integrates first-principles property predictions.
The proposed screening workflow integrates machine-learning property models.
Candidate compositions are screened under simulated high-temperature and mechanical-loading conditions.
Low calculated density is used as a screening criterion.
Predicted phase stability is used as a screening criterion.
Simulated mechanical response is used as a screening criterion.
The desired structural mediator is a single-phase or fine two-phase architecture, potentially containing nanoscale precipitates.
This optimized architecture promotes solid-solution strengthening and favorable dislocation mechanisms.
The workflow can identify composition regions retaining a stable BCC matrix while reducing alloy density.
Computational evaluation of large composition spaces can reduce reliance on empirical trial-and-error.
The workflow identifies compositions balancing reduced mass with sufficient dislocation mobility for ductility.
Screened RHEAs will exhibit significantly lower density after synthesis.
Screened RHEAs will maintain or enhance yield strength relative to conventionally designed refractory HEAs.
Screened RHEAs will maintain or enhance ductility relative to conventionally designed refractory HEAs.
The method's success is constrained by thermodynamic-database accuracy and machine-learning predictive accuracy.
Processing kinetics can produce phase evolution that is not fully represented by equilibrium simulations.
Conventional refractory HEAs are developed primarily through experimental trial-and-error or limited thermodynamic analysis.
